summary: Verified mobile Participants add-participant modal after wrapping in KeyboardAvoidingView + automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets. No regression: modal opens, preview step (family branch) renders correctly, Continue → 'Their details' form step renders all 4 inputs, typing into fields works (first_name='TestKB', last_name='Avoid'), the ScrollView is a real scrollable container (overflow-y:auto), close (add-modal-close) fully dismisses, and reopen shows a clean preview. Actual keyboard-occluding fix is a native effect that must be validated on-device (Expo web preview cannot fully reproduce software keyboard behaviour).

critical_code_review_comments: participants.tsx L274: KeyboardAvoidingView chosen behavior 'padding' for iOS / 'height' for Android is the standard recommendation — good.
participants.tsx L281: automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets on the inner ScrollView correctly complements KAV so nested inputs stay visible; keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' preserved.
Note (not a bug, deferred per request): the FORM step still uses free-text TextInputs for Classification and Provider — the tester was told NOT to test dropdown parity there (separate upcoming item).

Note: no keyboardVerticalOffset is set on KeyboardAvoidingView. On iOS with a translucent header/navigation bar this can leave ~44-88px of the field still under the keyboard. Not blocking (the modal is a bottom-sheet inside a native Modal so there is no parent header), but worth confirming on a real device — if the user still reports occlusion on iOS, add keyboardVerticalOffset={0} or a small platform-specific offset.

rca of the issue: Original issue: bottom-sheet Modal for add-participant had no keyboard avoidance, so on device the software keyboard overlapped the input fields. Fix (already applied by main agent): wrap the Modal's content container in KeyboardAvoidingView with platform-appropriate behavior and add automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets + paddingBottom to the inner ScrollView. This test iteration confirms the wrapper does not break rendering, focus, typing, scrolling, close, or reopen of the modal.
